query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small amount of a refractory metal dopant, such as tantalum (Ta), into the W–Cu composite will reduce phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix.
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount (e.g., 1–3 wt%) of tantalum (Ta) to the W–Cu composite.
generation.conditions: Heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced interfacial bonding and reduced void formation at the W-Cu interface due to the presence of Ta.
generation.mechanism: Tantalum acts as a stabilizing agent at the W-Cu interface, reducing the driving force for phase separation and mitigating the formation of interfacial voids by improving atomic-scale bonding and reducing diffusional mismatch under thermal and irradiation stresses.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Ta-doped W–Cu composite will exhibit higher thermal conductivity compared to the untreated composite under the specified conditions.
generation.baseline: Thermal conductivity of the untreated W–Cu composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.boundary: Applicable to W–Cu composites with W content in the range of 50–90 vol% and Cu content in the range of 10–50 vol%, processed via powder metallurgy or similar methods, and subjected to heat-transfer and irradiation conditions typical of plasma-facing material joints.
generation.uncertainty: The exact extent of thermal conductivity improvement and the optimal Ta concentration are uncertain due to the lack of direct experimental data.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare W–Cu composites with and without 1–3 wt% Ta doping using identical processing methods. Subject both materials to heat-transfer and irradiation conditions representative of plasma-facing material joints. Measure thermal conductivity and analyze microstructural changes, including interfacial bonding and void formation.
measurements: Void fraction at the W-Cu interface
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ta-doped W–Cu composite does not show a statistically significant improvement in thermal conductivity or if interfacial void formation is not reduced compared to the untreated composite, the hypothesis will be falsified.
